arxiv-2111-08483.title: Lattice-free simplices with lattice width 2 ​ d − o ⁡ ( d ) 2d-o(d)
arxiv-2111-08483.creator: Lukas Mayrhofer, Jamico Schade, Stefan Weltge
arxiv-2111-08483.description: Abstract The Flatness theorem states that the maximum lattice width Flt ⁡ ( d ) \mathrm{Flt}(d) of a d d -dimensional lattice-free convex set is finite. It is the key ingredient for Lenstra’s algorithm for integer programming in fixed dimension, and much work has been done to obtain bounds on Flt ⁡ ( d ) \mathrm{Flt}(d) .

arxiv-2202-08343.title: First exit time for a discrete time parallel queue
arxiv-2202-08343.creator: Zbigniew Palmowski
arxiv-2202-08343.description: Abstract 1 Introduction We consider a discrete time parallel queue, which is a two-queue network, with batch arrivals and services. At the beginning of the n th time-slot, A_{n} customers arrive to both queues. Then after this, S_{n}^{i}\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\} customers can be served in slot n by server i for i=1,2 .

arxiv-2305-11127.title: Unfaulting mechanisms of Frank loops in fluorite oxides
arxiv-2305-11127.creator: Miaomiao Jin, Jilang Miao, Yongfeng Zhang, Marat Khafizov, Kaustubh K. Bawane, Boopathy Kombaiah, David H. Hurley
arxiv-2305-11127.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Miaomiao Jin, Jilang Miao, Yongfeng Zhang, Marat Khafizov, Kaustubh K. Bawane, Boopathy Kombaiah, David H. Hurley. Unfaulting of Frank loops in irradiated fluoride oxides are of significance to microstructural evolution. However, the mechanisms have not been directly observed. To this end, we utilize molecular dynamics to reveal the atomistic details related to the unfaulting process of interstitial Frank loop in ThO 2 , which involve nucleation of single or multiple Shockley partial pairs at the loop circumference.

arxiv-2306-07008.title: Quantum Phase Estimation by Compressed Sensing
arxiv-2306-07008.creator: Changhao Yi, Cunlu Zhou, Jun Takahashi
arxiv-2306-07008.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Changhao Yi, Cunlu Zhou, Jun Takahashi. As a signal recovery algorithm, compressed sensing is particularly effective when the data has low complexity and samples are scarce, which aligns natually with the task of quantum phase estimation (QPE) on early fault-tolerant quantum computers. In this work, we present a new Heisenberg-limited, robust QPE algorithm based on compressed sensing, which requires only sparse and discrete sampling of times.

arxiv-2401-08368.title: How cytoskeletal crosstalk makes cells move: bridging cell-free and cell studies
arxiv-2401-08368.creator: James P. Conboy, Irene Istúriz Petitjean, Anouk van der Net, Gijsje H. Koenderink
arxiv-2401-08368.description: Abstract Cell migration is a fundamental process for life and is highly dependent on the dynamical and mechanical properties of the cytoskeleton. Intensive physical and biochemical crosstalk between actin, microtubules, and intermediate filaments ensures their coordination to facilitate and enable migration.

arxiv-2411-09434.title: Mediffusion: Joint Diffusion for Self-Explainable Semi-Supervised Classification and Medical Image Generation
arxiv-2411-09434.creator: Joanna Kaleta, Paweł Skierś, Jan Dubiński, Przemysław Korzeniowski, Kamil Deja
arxiv-2411-09434.description: Abstract We introduce Mediffusion – a new method for semi-supervised learning with explainable classification based on a joint diffusion model. The medical imaging domain faces unique challenges due to scarce data labelling – insufficient for standard training, and critical nature of the applications that require high performance, confidence, and explainability of the models.

arxiv-2508-18152.title: Optical Signatures of Band Flatness and Anisotropic Quantum Geometry in Magic-Angle Twisted Bilayer Graphene
arxiv-2508-18152.creator: Pok Man Chiu
arxiv-2508-18152.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pok Man Chiu. We study the degree of band flatness and the anisotropic quantum geometry in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene by varying the twist angle and the parameters of lattice relaxation using optical conductivity. We show that the degree of band flatness and its quantum geometry can be revealed through optical absorption and its resulting optical bounds, which are based on the trace condition in quantum geometry.

arxiv-2509-02477.title: HyDeFuse: Provably Convergent Denoiser-Driven Hyperspectral Fusion
arxiv-2509-02477.creator: Sagar Kumar, Unni V. S, Kunal N. Chaudhury
arxiv-2509-02477.description: Abstract Hyperspectral (HS) images provide fine spectral resolution but have limited spatial resolution, whereas multispectral (MS) images capture finer spatial details but have fewer bands. HS-MS fusion aims to integrate HS and MS images to generate a single image with improved spatial and spectral resolution. This is commonly formulated as an inverse problem with a linear forward model.

arxiv-2512-23708.title: Quantum Geometric Bounds in Non-Hermitian Systems
arxiv-2512-23708.creator: Milosz Matraszek, Wojciech J. Jankowski, Jan Behrends
arxiv-2512-23708.description: Abstract We identify quantum geometric bounds for observables in non-Hermitian systems. We find unique bounds on non-Hermitian quantum geometric tensors, generalized two-point response correlators, conductivity tensors, and optical weights. We showcase these findings in topological systems with non-Hermitian Chern numbers.

pmc-12569646.creator: Sofía Orioli, Javier Santos, Lorena I. Ibañez, Cecilia D’Alessio
pmc-12569646.description: IntroductionNanobodies (NBs) are small antibody fragments derived from camelid heavy-chain antibodies, which represent the minimal functional domain capable of antigen recognition and binding. NBs are 10 times smaller than conventional antibodies, exhibit a compact structure, and have high stability, making them ideal for recombinant production.

pmc-12685887.title: Plug-and-play high-frequency feature enhancement for plant image super-resolution
pmc-12685887.creator: Ling Xu, Bin Qiu, Huijun Xu, Xiaoli Zhu
pmc-12685887.description: IntroductionHigh-resolution plant imagery is vital for phenotyping, disease monitoring, and precision agriculture. However, image acquisition in real-world conditions is frequently limited by sensor resolution, cost, and environmental noise, resulting in low-quality images. While deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) approaches show promise, they often fail to recover fine structural details that are essential for plant science applications.
